translations.title: What Is Loved When One Loves, My God…
translations.text:
What is loved when one loves, my God:

The terrible light of life, or the light of death?

What is sought, what found, what is it?

Love? Who is it? The woman with her depths, her roses, her volcanoes,

Or this red sun that is my furious blood

When I enter her to the deepest roots?


Or is everything one great game, my God, and there is no woman

Nor man, but only one body: yours,

Scattered in stars of beauty, in fleeting particles

Of visible eternity?


I die in this, O God, in this war

Of going back and forth among them in the streets, of being unable to love

Three hundred at once, because I am always condemned to one,

To that one, that only one you gave me in the old paradise.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Always, Farewell
translations.text:
You will weep oceans,

three dark days, already pulverized

by my memory, by my fixed eyes

that will watch you weep behind your bedroom curtains,

unmoved, like two thorns,

because the thorn is the flower of nothingness.

And you will weep for me without knowing why you weep,

without knowing who has gone:

whether it is you, whether it is me, whether the abyss is a kiss.


Everything will happen all at once,

like your tears falling over my empty face.

You will run through the streets. You will look at me without seeing me

in the backs of all the men walking to work.

You will enter cinemas to hear me in the shadow of the murmur. You will open

the clattering door: there the tables will be waiting for my laughter,

as hoarse as the beer glass, served and desolate.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Accomplices
translations.text:
I told you in the letter

that putting four lines together

was no passport to happiness
stamped in your pocket,

and other more or less serious things,

as if to let you know

that since long ago I have been your accomplice

when you descend to the arsenals of night

and put your whole soul

and breath,

perfectly controlled,

to keep your rebellions standing,
your secret militias,

at the cost of all that time lost

biting your nails, keeping
your heartbeats in check,

beating your chest over bad dreams,

and I don’t know how many other things

that, frankly, wear down your health,

when deep down

you know I am with you,

even if I do not see you

or eat breakfast at your table

nor wake with my head on your chest

like a cold child,

and that need not be written.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Electric, Naked on the Burning Marble…
translations.text:
Electric, naked on the burning marble that passes from skin to clothes,

turgid, defiant, the tide swift,

they tread the world, tread the lucky star in their fine heels

and germinate, germinate like wild plants in the street,

and give off their hard green scent.


Warm, intangible girls of the summer that buzzes like a butcher. Neither roses

nor archangels: girls of this country, diviners

of man, and something more than shimmering heat,

something more, something more than these supple branches

that know what they know as the earth knows.


So light, so deep, so sure, the gentle ones. A hunt

of blue eyes and other urgent flares in the dance

of swift streets. Females, females

in the hoarse swell where we cast the nets of our five senses

to draw out barely the kiss of foam.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Suicide Note
translations.text:
I swear this woman has split my brains,

because she comes and goes like a mad bullet,

and opens my parietal bones, and they never heal,

whether summer blows or winter,

whether I live happily, seated on triumph

and full-bellied, like a sated condor,

whether I suffer hunger’s lash, whether I lie down

or rise, and plunge headfirst into the day

like a stone beneath the shifting current,

whether I touch my lyre to deceive myself, whether

a door opens and ten naked women enter,

their backs marked with my script, and they throw themselves

one upon another until they are spent,

I swear she endures, because she comes and goes

like a mad bullet,

follows me wherever I go and serves as my fairy,

kisses me lustfully

trying to escape death,

and, when I fall asleep, lodges in my spinal

column and cries out to me for help,

snatches me to the heavens, like a motherless condor

hatched in death.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Like the Blind Man Weeping Against a Pitiless Sun…
translations.text:
Like the blind man weeping against a pitiless sun,

I persist in seeing light through my empty eyes,

burned forever.


What use is the ray

that writes through my hand? What use is fire,

if I have lost my eyes?


What use is the world to me?


What use is the body that makes me eat,

and sleep, and take pleasure, if everything comes down

to feeling pleasures in the dark,

to biting breasts and lips,

the shapes of death?


Two wombs bore me, I was cast

into the world by two mothers, conceived in two,

and the mystery was doubled, but the fruit was one

of that monstrous birth.


There are two tongues inside my mouth,

two heads inside my skull:

two men in my body endlessly devour each other,

two skeletons fight to be one spine.


I have no word but my mouth

to speak of myself,

my stammering tongue

that names half my visions

beneath the lucidity

of my own torment, like the blind man weeping

against a pitiless sun.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Fornication
translations.text:
I will kiss you on the tips of your lashes and on your nipples,

I will kiss you turbulently, my shy one,

on those thighs of a white woman,

I would touch those feet for a flight with more air

than the feline air of your fragrance.

I would call you my Spanish girl, my French girl,

English, ragazza, boreal northerner,

foam from Genesis’s diaspora.

What else would I tell you within?

Greek, my Egyptian, Roman as marble?

Phoenician, Carthaginian, or mad,

madly Andalusian in the arch of dying

with every petal open,

God’s lyre taut in the dance of fornication?

I would hear you howl, I would bite you

to the last poppies, my possessed one,

I would still drive you mad there, in blind coolness,

I would swim you in lust’s insatiable immensity,

my frenzy would laugh frantically with your teeth,

your skin’s opium would snatch me to another purity’s ivory,

I would hear the bursting spheres sing like Pythagoras,

lick you, scent you like a lion his lioness,

for the sun, I would love you as mine, phallically!
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: For Vallejo
translations.text:
Everything had already been written when Vallejo said: “Still.”

And he tore this feather from the old condor

of emphasis. Time is still;

the rose is still, and though summer pass, and the stars

of every summer, man is still.


Nothing happened. But someone named César, in Peruvian,

and in stone more than stone, reached the summit

of beautiful oxygen. The roots

followed him, bleeding, ever more lucid each day. They went

drying him out, and not even Paris could save his bones or his martyrdom.


No one went so deep through the living marrow of origin,

nor spoke to us in the music we call America,

for he alone drew being from the darkest stone

when he saw our fate beneath the waves,

in the hollow of the hand.


Each has his own Vallejo, grieving and glad.

Not in Paris,

where I wept for his soul, not in the violent cloud

that at ten thousand meters gave me earthly certainty of his face

above the open snow, but here,

in breathing the mortal thorn, I am sure

of the one who descends and tells me: “Still.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Come
translations.text:
Take deep within you the little Chinese bell,
and when the lilac comes,
		blend this too
with your blood, your joy and your misery,
with the
		dark ground on which you depend.


Slow days. All things passed.
And you do not ask whether beginning or end,

		then perhaps the hours will carry you
still into June, with its
		roses.
Translated
		by Eustaquio Barjau
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Farewell
translations.text:
Last Spring

		Take deep within you the little Chinese bell,
and when the lilac comes,
		blend this too
with your blood, your joy and your misery,
with the
		dark ground on which you depend.


Slow days. All things passed.
And you do not ask whether beginning or end,

		then perhaps the hours will carry you
still into June, with its
		roses.
Translated
		by Eustaquio Barjau
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Water or Dream, Part Two
translations.text:
Swallowing the sea, breathing blue water,
		cleansing with its salt the sick lungs
		of that tar of tedium that traps some
		beings who write to one another and bargain with death,
		and you must stand on the same ledge
		of stone, in the same crack
		of the glass, to understand.


		But they leave their reddened wake
		only for the others;
		for many of them there is no tragedy,
		only the desire to cut the final
		thread,
		to leave the world’s cage,
		only the last pulse, the fevered instant
		of unmasking her, of looking into her eyes.


		Only wanting to be a silent sea,
		the waves
		shearing off the thorns of anguish,
		giving the root of the voice
		to the cave of words;
		only to be a pill, a fortress of rest,
		dissolve consciousness,
		flood memory, be nothing.


		foam, foam
From the
		book The Song of the Lovers, Barcelona, 2006
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Beneath the Mantle of Stars
translations.text:

		Swallowing the sea, breathing blue water,

		beings who write to one another and bargain with death,

translations.title: I Am Going to Buy a Whip
translations.text:
I am going to buy a whip

Of yellow pigskin

If I cannot find one

I will take my coachman’s whip
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: North and South
translations.text:
North and South

Zenith, Nadir

And the great cries of the East

The Ocean swells in the West

The Tower toward the Wheel

Sets out
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Hours Pass Slowly
translations.text:
The hours pass slowly

Like a funeral procession

You will weep for the hour in which you weep

Which too will flee swiftly

As all the hours pass
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Farewell
translations.text:
I picked this sprig of heather

Autumn has died, remember

We shall meet no more upon the earth

Scent of time, sprig of heather

And remember I am waiting for you
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Epigram
translations.text:
My lovely gardener

You who wanted to know why

No one strikes you on the behind

You know, as I do,

That one must not strike a woman


Not even with a Rare Flower, yes, ma’am
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: When Two Noble Hearts Have Truly Loved
translations.text:
When two noble hearts have truly loved

Their love is stronger than death itself

Let us gather the memories we have sown

And absence, after all, is nothing when one loves
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: And Take Great Care of the Zeppelins
translations.text:
And take great care of the Zeppelins

Of Zeppelins of every kind

Those of the Boches are not bad

The French ones are much fuller

And take great care of the Zeppelins

Every French officer carries one
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Prisoner Without a Horizon
translations.text:
Prisoner without a horizon

I hear the noises of the street

And see only a hostile sky

And the white wall of my prison


Evening flees through my cell

A sweet lamp burns

We are alone in my cell

Beautiful light, beloved reason
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Photograph
translations.text:
Your smile attracts me as

A flower would attract me


Photograph, you are the dark fungus

Of the jungle

Which is its beauty

The whites are there

Moonlight

In a peaceful garden

Full of living waters and devilish gardeners


Photograph, you are the smoke of ardor

Which is its beauty

And there are in you

Photograph

Languid tones

Where one hears

A melody


Photograph, you are the shadow

Of the Sun

Which is its beauty.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Before the Cinema
translations.text:
And then this evening we shall go

To the cinema


Today’s Artists

Are no longer those who cultivate the Fine Arts

They are not the ones concerned with Art

Poetic or musical Art

Artists are actors and actresses


If we were Artists

We would not say cinema

We would say cine


But if we were old provincial professors

We would say neither cine nor cinema

But cinematograph


My God, one must also have good taste.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I Had the Courage to Look Back
translations.text:
I had the courage to look back

The corpses of my days

Mark my path, and I weep for them

Some rot in Italian churches

Or in little lemon groves

That blossom and bear fruit

At once, in every season

Other days wept before they died in taverns

Where burning bouquets rolled

Before the eyes of a mulatta who invented poetry

And the roses of electricity still open

In the garden of my memory
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Amid the Murmur of the Bells
translations.text:
Amid the murmur of the bells,

beautiful gypsy, my beloved,

we loved each other madly

and no one, no one saw us.


We forgot that the bells,

leaning from the belfry,

saw us, alas, and night and day

tell the whole neighborhood.


Tomorrow Pedro and Catalina,

the baker and his wife,

Juan and María Golondrina,

my friend Luz, my cousin Ester,


will smile in a certain way…

I shall not know where to hide…

You will be far away… I shall weep…

And it is even possible I shall die…
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Courtship
translations.text:
Spring lets the faithless lovers wander

and the blue feathers shaken by the cypress,

where the blue bird nests, flutter like leaves.


At dawn a Madonna gathered wild roses

and tomorrow she will come for the wallflowers

to place them in the dove nests she has set aside

for that pigeon which at dusk seemed the Paraclete.


In the little lemon grove they fell in love

with the love with which we love the last to arrive.

Distant villages are like eyelids

And among the lemons their hearts hang suspended.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Words of Love to Linda
translations.text:
Your name, a little pretentious, very pagan,

because it is yours, I find delightful.

In Spanish it means “pretty,” and since you are,

every time it is spoken, the truth is told.


In German that name turns melancholy;

in April’s breeze it murmurs sweetly.

It is a lyrical lime tree, a tree of legend,

from which each night a flock of elves flies out.


At last, that strange name that speaks your beauty

was also the name of a Greek city

that blossomed among Rhodes’ lovely roses,

the island where young doves coo.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Fill My Glass with Wine, Trembling Like a Flame
translations.text:
Fill my glass with wine, trembling like a flame.

Listen to the boatman’s slow song

About seven women seen upon the moon,

braiding their long green hair.


Sing standing, louder, as you dance the round,

so I no longer hear the boatman sing,

and bring the fair-haired girls near me,

with steady eyes and braided hair.


The Rhine, the Rhine is drunk where vineyards gaze;

all the night’s gold trembles, reflected there.

In its agony the voice forever sings of these fairies

whose green hair bewitches summer.


My glass has shattered like a laugh.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.
